title: What If Every Atom Gained One Extra Electron?
description:
Adding one electron sounds tiny—but doing it to every atom would be catastrophic.

Matter would acquire an enormous negative charge; electrostatic repulsion and rapid electron loss would dominate, making the setup physically impossible to maintain.

Many atoms cannot stably bind an extra electron, and charge would discharge into the surroundings long before a uniform state existed.

Electrostatic forces between charged objects can vastly exceed gravity at atomic and everyday scales.
